quotes.speaker: Stephanie
quotes.summary_phrase: The slow, intentional process of falling in love with Jesus
quotes.excerpt: it was a slow process because it's also a slow process to fall in love with someone

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: It sounds like you're saying it was a slow process because it's also a slow process to fall in love with someone and fall in love with Jesus. The more you love him, he kind of, you know, how does someone then, if they are wanting to try it out like you did, how do you fall in love with Jesus?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephanie
text_blocks.text: I would say two things. Number one, reading the Bible and having, dating Jesus. When you're getting to know someone, you're not like, okay, I'm going to erase every number in my phone and I'm never going to go on another date. Like, no, you talk to them, you get to know them. And so, having a two-way conversation with God every day. So, praying is us talking to God, and a lot of people pray, they like to talk, but they don't listen. Reading is us listening and God talking back. And so, making it our goal to have a two-way conversation with God every day because that's how you fall in love with somebody, that's how you get to know them.

quotes.speaker: Stephanie
quotes.summary_phrase: Living a life as a sacrifice to God for transformation
quotes.excerpt: making our life a living sacrifice and that being our true and proper worship
quotes.quote: Romans 12:1 and 2 talks about making our life a living sacrifice and that being our true and proper worship. And when we do that, our mind will be renewed and transformed. And so, there is an aspect, it's not just about, okay, I'm going to read and pray and see what happens. No, there is an aspect of self-denial, of I'm going to try my absolute best to live in accordance with what God is calling me to do, and in that process, my mind will be renewed and transformed.

quotes.speaker: Stephanie
quotes.summary_phrase: The necessity of grace when falling short of God's standards
quotes.excerpt: there is grace for when you fall short. Now, grace doesn't cover us just wailing
quotes.quote: There is also the scripture that you mentioned earlier, Romans 7, where Paul is like, the good I know to do, that I do not do, and the bad I want to do, I keep on doing. And then right after that, in Romans 8:1, it says, now there is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. And so, it's in context of that, and so what I would say to anyone trying to completely change their lifestyle is like, yeah, have a two-way conversation with God every day, yes, make this your true and proper worship, your life is a living sacrifice, but understand that there is grace for when you fall short. Now, grace doesn't cover us just wailing and continuing to live this lifestyle like everyone pretends it does. No, grace means that our human best is good enough for a perfect God.

quotes.speaker: Stephanie
quotes.summary_phrase: Advice for those struggling with God's demands on their lifestyle
quotes.excerpt: just get to know him because you're so loved. You're so loved
quotes.quote: I hear that a lot actually. I hear that a lot. I was like, if that's what God is going to ask of me, then I'm not going to do it. That I don't even want to get to know a God that would want that from me, or that would demand that from me. And that could be anything, not just sexuality, but anything else. And what I would tell somebody is just get to know him because you're so loved. You're so loved, and obeying a loving God and submitting your life to him in every aspect is the best self-love and self-care you can ever do. If you love yourself, you will truly submit to a loving God.

quotes.speaker: Stephanie
quotes.summary_phrase: Why Christianity is the path to God over other religions

quotes.quote: Initially, I think it's just because I grew up around Christianity. So, I think as I've gotten more into my walk with God and I've done more research on other religions and things like that, Jesus is God, and Muhammad didn't die for my sins, neither did Buddha. They didn't raise from the dead either, they're still dead. They're all dead, and Jesus is not. So, it was a very, that's not a hard question, but man, when you preach the gospel to that, to that Muslim guy, that was so amazing, but it's just like, it offends so many people. Jesus is the way, the truth, the life. No one comes to the Father except through me, and he's the only way.

quotes.speaker: Stephanie
quotes.summary_phrase: The modern craving for structure and biblical discipleship
quotes.excerpt: people are craving real structure. Tell me how I'm supposed to live this life
quotes.quote: I do think a lot of people are converting for that reason, both to Islam, and we're seeing a modern resurgence to Catholicism as well, and I think it's because people are craving real structure. People are craving, like, listen, tell me how I'm supposed to live this life because how I'm living it isn't going well. And Christianity provides that as well. The problem is that in Christianity, we have set the standard at belief, when Jesus set it at discipleship. If we look at the Bible, the word Christian is only in the Bible three times, and the word disciple is in the Bible over 270 times, almost 300 times. And so, the word Christian was actually a nickname for the disciples. It's like, your name is Michael, right? But people call you Mike. I'm talking about the same person, this is Mike Michael. Same with Christian and disciple. A Christian was a nickname for a disciple. Now, a disciple is a student or follower of some teacher. So, a disciple of Jesus means that I'm supposed to sit at his feet, learn everything he's telling me, and then I'm supposed to go out and be exactly like him. Well, if a Christian is just a nickname for a disciple, then that's the standard of biblical Christianity. It's to live out discipleship, is obedience and following. And the culture has set it at, oh, I can be a Christian without being a disciple. I can be a Christian without obedience. I can be a Christian without following. And the Bible is like, no, we can't.

quotes.speaker: Stephanie
quotes.summary_phrase: Repentance as a change of mind leading to action
quotes.excerpt: repentance is a change of mind that leads to a change of action
quotes.quote: Repentance is a change of mind that leads to a change of action. It's changing my mind to agree with God about my sin, and because I agree with God, I don't live it any longer. That's repentance. It's not just feeling bad, it's not just believing. And so, repentance, if there's two powers of this world, right? There's God and there's Satan. Two powers. So, when we're, we're in the middle. When we are living a sinful lifestyle, who are we following? We're following Satan because there's only two powers. If you're not following God, you're following Satan. So, we're following Satan. Then we say, okay, I want to repent, I want to change my life. I'm going to change my mind to agree that this lifestyle is not what I should be living, and that change of mind is going to lead to a change of action. So, I'm going to turn around and I'm now going to follow Jesus with my life. Now, that's repentance. But what did I just become? I became a disciple, because I'm now a follower and student of Jesus instead of previously, a follower and student of Satan. So, repentance is becoming a disciple.

quotes.speaker: Stephanie
quotes.summary_phrase: The necessity of repentance in the church
quotes.excerpt: the church a lot of times is unsafe because we don't require repentance
quotes.quote: The church a lot of times is unsafe because we don't require repentance to be part of the church, as the Bible calls us to do. The church, a lot of times, is unsafe because we don't require repentance to be part of the church, as the Bible calls us to do.

quotes.speaker: Stephanie
quotes.summary_phrase: Navigating friendships while maintaining personal convictions
quotes.excerpt: they know I love them and they know I disagree with them
quotes.quote: I have several friends that are in the lifestyle still, and they know two things about me. They know I love them and they know I disagree with them. And either one, not knowing either one would be me betraying Jesus. Because they have to know I disagree with it, but they also know that I love them. And so, can I support their lifestyle in terms of agreement? No. Can I love them as being in their life? Absolutely. And but they have to know those two things. And what I've found is most people would not invite you into certain places if they know you disagree. And that's okay. But I have friends that, like, we hang out and they know how I feel and per their decision, we don't talk about it always or whatever, but they know where I stand and they know that I'm here if they ever want to seek a deeper relationship with God.

quotes.speaker: Stephanie

quotes.quote: Again, same-sex attraction is not a sin. Acting on it is a sin.
